did_you_know.text: Did you know? The phrase "after this" presents the outpouring of the Spirit as an event that will occur after an earlier stage, without specifying here how long that stage will last or when it will occur.
Did you know? According to the verse, the LORD’s Spirit will be poured out on "all flesh"—an expression emphasizing the broad scope and universal nature of the promise.
Did you know? The prophecy includes different age groups and genders: sons and daughters will prophesy, old men will dream dreams, and young men will see visions.
Did you know? The promise is not limited to free people or to a particular social class: male and female servants are also explicitly mentioned as those on whom the LORD’s Spirit will be poured out.
Did you know? Before the day of the LORD, signs are described both in the heavens and on the earth, including blood, fire, and columns of smoke.
Did you know? The description of the sun being darkened and the moon turning to blood uses vivid cosmic imagery to portray the approach of the great and awesome day of the LORD.

Did you know? The verse presents a principle of deliverance: everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will escape. At the same time, it mentions deliverance on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, as well as among the survivors whom the LORD calls.

Did you know? The word "deliverance" in the verse is connected to the idea of survivors who have been rescued. The text does not describe only general salvation; it also mentions a group that remains and is called by the LORD.
